lead: On a boat everything has its own name, and the skipper's orders are made of those names. Learn where things are, which side the wind is on and what the main parts are called, and you will understand an order the first time you hear it.

sections.title: Left and right belong to the boat

qa.q: Is port still the left side of the boat when I'm facing the stern?
qa.a: Yes: **port** is the left side and starboard the right as seen facing the bow, whichever way you look. Sitting in the cockpit facing aft, you have the port side on your right.

blocks.p: **Port** is the left side of the boat and **starboard** the right, as seen by someone facing the bow. They do not change when you turn round: sitting in the cockpit facing aft, you have the port side on your right. The **bow** is the front and the **stern** the back; **forward** means towards the bow, **aft** towards the stern.

fig.note: Named from the boat, facing forward

blocks.p: The same words say where something is around you. A boat level with you, at right angles to your own, is **abeam**. Between abeam and astern lies the **quarter**, between abeam and ahead the bow. So you report "motor yacht abeam to starboard" or "wind over the port quarter".

blocks.rule: Port and starboard are named facing forward, wherever you are looking.

sections.title: Which side the wind is on

qa.q: How do I tell which side of the boat is windward?
qa.a: Look at the boom: the wind pushes it away, so it always lies to leeward. With the boom out over starboard, port is the **windward** side, the one the wind comes from.

blocks.p: The **windward** side is the one the wind comes from, the **leeward** side the one it blows towards. The wind pushes the boom away from it, so the boom always lies to leeward: see it out over the starboard side and you know that port is windward.

fig.note: Wind from starboard: the boom is out to port

blocks.p: The crew sits to windward, to balance the heel. Whatever goes over the side, a bucket of washing-up water included, goes to leeward, or the wind brings it back aboard.
**In the lee** of something means sheltered by it. With a north wind the lee of an island is its south side: flat water for the night.

fig.note: Wind N 20 kn, sea from the north

sections.title: From the keel to the companionway

qa.q: Where does water collect inside a sailing boat, and what is that space called?
qa.a: In the **bilge**, the lowest space inside the hull, under the floorboards. That is where you look when the skipper asks you to check it.

blocks.p: The **keel** is the heavy fin under the hull that keeps the boat upright. It is her deepest part, so it is the first to touch the bottom. The **rudder** is the steering blade right aft, just behind the propeller.

blocks.p: Water that gets inside collects in the **bilge**, so that is where you look when the skipper asks you to check it. When waves start to slop into the cockpit, the **washboards** go in.

qa.q: What are the wires that hold up a sailing boat's mast called?
qa.a: The **forestay** runs from the masthead to the bow, the backstay to the stern, and the shrouds down to the deck on each side, held away from the mast by the spreaders.

blocks.p: Steel wires hold the mast up. The **forestay** runs from the masthead to the bow, the **backstay** to the stern, and the **shrouds** go down to the deck on each side, held away from the mast by the **spreaders**. A roller-furling genoa rolls up round the forestay.

Under sail the windward shroud carries the load. After a tack the other one takes over, so a missing split pin or a broken strand on the slack side matters just as much: tell the skipper before the boat tacks.
Flags have their places too. The boat's own ensign flies at the stern, and the **courtesy flag** of the country you are visiting is hoisted under the starboard spreader.

qa.q: How do I work out how much water there is under the keel?
qa.a: If the sounder shows the depth below the waterline, take the **draft** off it: 2.6 m on the sounder minus a 2.1 m draft leaves 0.5 m. Some sounders show the depth under the keel directly.

blocks.p: The depth the boat needs is her draft plus a margin. If the depth sounder shows the depth below the waterline, take the draft off to find what is left under the keel. Ask the skipper how the sounder is set: some show the depth under the keel directly.
